subject: Horizon Bank: On-prem deployment KMS/HSM and network safeguards

Subject: On-prem deployment KMS/HSM + network safeguards kickoff

Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As we prepare our on-prem pilot for Redwood Private, InfoSec would like to validate the key management and network isolation approach before contract finalization. High-level asks below:

- Confirm BYOK key custody model (HSM vs KMS proxy), evidence you can provide for key provenance and attestation.
- Outline key rotation cadence and emergency unseal/eviction playbook for operator compromise.
- Network zoning: firewall rules, inter-VLAN flow, and allowed egress for the KMS/HSM control plane.
- Requirements for audit logs, retention windows, and how we can export signed evidence for audits (SOC2).

Attached is a short spreadsheet with their initial questionnaire. We'd like a short readout and a proposed acceptance checklist by EOD Thursday.

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment KMS/HSM + network safeguards kickoff

Julia —

Appreciate the questionnaire. We can provide the evidence and a concrete acceptance checklist. High-level commitment and plan from our side:

1) Custody model: Redwood supports two patterns for Private on-prem customers:
   - Customer HSM-first BYOK: your HSM (FIPS 140-2/3 validated) holds the root signing keys; Redwood runs a local KMS proxy that never stores unwrapped root key material.
   - Redwood-hosted sealed HSM (for air-gapped customers): we deploy a sealed HSM appliance that we attest and hand back key material under a split-operator ceremony.

   For Horizon pilot we recommend Customer HSM-first BYOK to meet your regulatory controls. We will provide: attestation artifacts (HSM serial + signer certs), nonce-based challenge logs, and a signed proof-of-possession bundle.

2) Rotation and emergency: propose quarterly automated rotation for wrapping keys, annual asymmetric root rollover, plus a documented emergency unseal/eviction playbook. We'll produce a rehearsable runbook and a checklist for operators and auditors.

3) Network zoning: recommended pattern is a dedicated KMS VLAN with explicit deny-by-default egress; management plane only on a bastion jump host with strict CIDR rules. Our diagram (attached) shows the crossconnects; we'll suggest firewall templates and MTU/QoS notes.

4) Audit logs: we provide immutably signed log bundles (daily) and short-term streaming to your collector (S3-compatible endpoint in your VPC), plus long-term sealed archives. Retention windows are configurable — default 1 year for audit-ready bundles.

I'll attach a proposed network diagram and a rotation matrix for your team to review. Vanessa will lead the technical review; Karthik will own operational acceptance criteria.

Next steps: Vanessa/Karthik — can you draft the acceptance checklist (security + ops) and note any blocking controls by Wednesday EOD? Julia — we'll propose a 45 min walkthrough Thursday morning PST if that works.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_onprem_kms_network_diagram_v1.pdf] [Attachment: rotation_matrix_proposal.csv]

Best,

Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment KMS/HSM + network safeguards kickoff

Julia / team —

Thanks, Sean. Uploaded a draft acceptance checklist and a concise operator playbook to the drive link (see related_links). Summary of items I expect Horizon to validate during pilot (short checklist):

- BYOK proof: deliverable = signed PoP bundle including HSM serial, signer cert chain, challenge response, and measurement summary.
- Operator separation: acceptance = dual-operator ceremony documented and replayable (test scenario logs).
- Network isolation: acceptance = KMS VLAN cannot reach internet except to approved collector IPs; NATs disallowed; firewall rules exported for audit.
- Egress gating: acceptance = only S3-compatible collector allowed; ports 443/tcp and only to provided endpoints.
- Rotation verification: deliverable = rotation_matrix_proposal.csv with cron schedule and automated test that verifies token revocation + key unwrap success.
- Emergency unseal: acceptance = runbook execution within 30 minutes by designated ops (tabletop test).
- Audit/export: acceptance = signed log bundle for a sample day and proof it can be imported to your SIEM.

Notes and deviations:
- We strongly advise using an on-prem HSM (Luna/Elliptic) for your root. If you cannot, we have a sealed-HSM operator model but it increases operational windows.
- For MTU-sensitive networks (financial wire engines), we'll recommend tuning in the diagram (page 2).

I've also attached a short example rotation test script we run in staging (script referenced in rotation_matrix_proposal.csv). We'll also surface a small set of requirements we need from Horizon infra (jump host IPs, collector credentials, KMS VLAN CIDR, and HSM admin RSA public key).

Attachment references included in doc: [Attachment: rotation_matrix_proposal.csv]

Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick operational note and acceptance criteria addendum —

Thanks for the checklist, Vanessa. Two operational items I'd like Horizon to confirm before the walkthrough:

1) RTO/RPO expectations for key material: we propose an RTO of 1 hour for ephemeral service keys and 8 hours for root reconstruction (with an operator ceremony). If those are acceptable we'll codify retention and snapshot cadence in the runbook.

2) Test harness access: to run the rotation verification we need a temporary service account with scoped access to your collector bucket and a temporary CIDR allowance for our test harness (will be removed after tests). We issue short-lived credentials and log all calls.

Acceptance gate notes (will be part of the formal checklist):
- Gate A: Evidence of PoP bundle validated by Horizon Security (pass/fail).
- Gate B: Successful rotation test (automated) with logs ingested into Horizon SIEM.
- Gate C: Tabletop emergency unseal executed and time-to-unseal measured.

If these gates are green we can mark Pilot-Ready and schedule the Thursday walkthrough at 11:00 PST (Julian — please confirm).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
